diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a simple consequence of the fact that $X + BY$ is Gaussian and there is an affine transport map between any two non-singular Gaussians.
However, there are infinitely many other affine  conditioning maps $L_{\pi, y_\star}(x,y)=A(\pi,y_\star)x + B(\pi, y_\star)y + c(\pi, y_\star)$ that are exact for Gaussians.

issues.failure_explanation: For jointly Gaussian $(X,Y)$, exactness of $\ell(x,y)=Ax+By+c$ at $y_\star$ forces $\Cov(AX+BY)=\Sigma_{X|Y}$. In the scalar case $\Sigma_X=\Sigma_Y=1$, $\Sigma_{XY}=\rho$ this reads $A^2+B^2+2AB\rho=1-\rho^2$, which has a real solution $A$ iff $|B|\le 1$. For $\rho=0.5$ and $B=-2$ one has $\Cov(X-2Y)=3>0$ (so the parenthetical 'full rank' holds) but $A^2-2A+3.25=0$ has discriminant $-9<0$, so no exact affine map with $y$-coefficient $-2$ exists. The cited construction (affine transport from $\Law(X+BY)$ to the Gaussian posterior) produces maps $T(x+By)$ whose $y$-coefficient is $\alpha B$ with $\alpha\neq 1$ generically, not $B$. Thus 'for every choice of $B$' is false; the correct statement is that a restricted one-parameter family of $y$-coefficients is achievable, which still yields infinitely many exact maps.

failure_location.quote: For example, for every choice of $B$ (assuming $\Cov(X+BY)$ has full rank for all $y_\star$) there are $A$  and $c$ such that $L_{\pi,y_\star}(x,y)= A(\pi,y_\star)x + B(\pi, y_\star)y + c(\pi, y_\star)$ is exact.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the sentence to match the construction actually supported: for every $B$ with $\Cov(X+BY)$ full rank, the composite $(x,y)\mapsto T(x+By)$ (with $T$ an affine transport between the two Gaussians) is exact, i.e. maps of the form $Ax+ABy+c$; or state the necessary and sufficient covariance constraint on the $y$-coefficient.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction's specific characterization of the non-uniqueness of exact affine maps for Gaussian joints is wrong as stated; the surrounding narrative (infinitely many exact affine maps exist for Gaussians) and all formal results are unaffected.
issues.title: Introduction falsely claims every gain matrix B is realizable by an exact affine Gaussian update
issues.why_classification: A local rephrasing of one introductory sentence; the motivational claim (non-uniqueness of the exact affine update for Gaussians) and every formal result survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $\frac{\theta}{2\pi} \in \mathbb{Q}$ or $X$ is invariant under all rotations.
This is a contradiction to $\pi \not \in \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ and we must have $\lambda = 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:angle_rot concludes a disjunction: either $\theta/2\pi\in\mathbb{Q}$ or the random vector is invariant under all rotations. The proof of part (3) invokes the lemma to conclude rationality of $\theta/2\pi$ alone and then derives cyclic symmetry of order $t$; the second alternative (irrational $\theta$, invariance under all rotations) is never handled. In that unhandled case, the derived invariance $\overline Z_{cyc}\stackrel{d}{=}R_\theta\overline Z_{cyc}$ together with full rotational invariance would also give invariance under $R_{2\pi/k}$ for any $k\ge 2$ with the same nonzero $v_1=p_1$, $v_2=p_2$, hence $\pi\in\mathrm{S}_{cyc}$, so the theorem's conclusion stands, but the written inference is an invalid use of the lemma (a missing case of the case split).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing case: if $\theta/2\pi\notin\mathbb{Q}$, then by Lemma lem:angle_rot $\overline Z_{cyc}$ is invariant under all rotations, in particular under $R_{2\pi/k}$ for $k=2$ (or any $k\ge 2$), which again contradicts $\pi\notin\mathrm{S}_{cyc}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of part (3) of thm:enkf_update_unique, and hence the derivation of cor:enkf_char, is incomplete as written.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem enkf_update_unique(3) draws a conclusion Lemma angle_rot does not give
issues.why_classification: A two-sentence addition repairing one branch of a case split; the statement and all conclusions are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To rule out spurious constant offsets in the constant \(c\), we assume \(\Sigma_{YY}\) is invertible.
Next, we show that except for a small class of highly symmetric distributions within \(\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}\) (including Gaussians), the EnKU is the \emph{unique} exact affine conditioning map.

Further, we showed that within $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$, the EnKU is the unique affine  exact conditioning map up to small symmetry classes $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}}, \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{dec}},$ and $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ (Theorem \ref{thm:enkf_update_unique}).

issues.failure_explanation: Uniqueness is only established by cor:enkf_char under the additional hypothesis that $\Sigma_{YY}$ is non-singular. Without it the claim is false: take $n=m=1$, $Y\equiv 0$ a.s., and $X$ non-degenerate and non-symmetric with finite second moment; then $\pi\in\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$ (the EnKU is $x\mapsto x$ and $\pi_{X|Y=y}=\pi_X$ a.e.) and $\pi$ violates $\mathrm{S}_{cov}$, $\mathrm{S}_{dec}$, and $\mathrm{S}_{cyc}$, yet $\ell(x,y)=x+by$ is an exact affine conditioning map at $y_\star=0$ for every $b$ (since $\ell(X,Y)=X$ a.s.), so the EnKU is not the unique exact affine map. The abstract, Section 3, the figure caption, and the Discussion restate uniqueness without the non-singularity hypothesis (the Discussion also attributes it to thm:enkf_update_unique rather than the corollary).

failure_location.quote: The previous section established that, apart from a small symmetry class $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}} \cup \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{dec}}  \cup \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}} $, the Ensemble Kalman Update (EnKU) is the unique affine conditioning map that is exact for any element  $\pi \in\mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU}$ and observation $y_\star\in\R^m$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the non-singular $\Sigma_{YY}$ hypothesis (or the qualifier that uniqueness holds up to maps agreeing with the EnKU $\pi$-a.s.) to the abstract's, Section 3's, figure caption's, and Discussion's uniqueness claims, and cite the corollary rather than the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: Prose summaries (abstract, Section 3, Discussion, Figure caption) claim a stronger uniqueness result than the paper establishes; the formal results themselves are correctly stated under their hypotheses.
issues.title: Uniqueness of the EnKU asserted without the required non-singular $\Sigma_{YY}$ hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Local edits to prose restatements; the underlying formal result (cor:enkf_char) is correctly hypothesized and entirely unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\hat A\in \R^{n\times n}$ is therefore a matrix satisfying $$ \hat A \hat C_f\hat A^\top = \hat C_a $$
$( \hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1} H\hat X_f^{(c)}= C D C^T$  is the eigenvalue decomposition

issues.failure_explanation: With $CDC^\top$ the eigendecomposition of the unscaled matrix $(\hat X^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1}H\hat X^{(c)}$ and $\hat C_f=\frac{1}{N-1}\hat X^{(c)}\hat X^{(c)\top}$, the moment condition $\hat A\hat C_f\hat A^\top=\hat C_a$ forces the middle factor to involve $(I+D/(N-1))^{-1/2}$, since $I-\hat X^{(c)\top}H^\top(H\hat C_fH^\top+\Gamma)^{-1}H\hat X^{(c)}=(I+\frac{1}{N-1}CDC^\top)^{-1}$ (consistent with the paper's own ETKF condition on $\hat T$). The printed $(I+D)^{-1/2}$ gives instead $(I+D)^{-1}$, which does not satisfy the stated equation: e.g. in the scalar case $n=m=1$, $H=1$, $S=\sum_i x_i^2$, $\gamma=\Gamma$, one gets $\hat A^{(3)\,2}\hat C_f=\frac{S}{2}(1+S/\gamma)^{-1}$ whereas $\hat C_a=\frac{S\gamma}{S+2\gamma}$; inserting the factor $1/(N-1)$ on $D$ restores equality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the scaling, e.g. $\hat A^{(3)}=\hat X_f^{(c)}C(I+D/(N-1))^{-1/2}G^\dagger F^T$, or equivalently define $CDC^\top$ as the eigendecomposition of $\frac{1}{N-1}(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1}H\hat X_f^{(c)}$, and verify the moment condition $\hat A\hat C_f\hat A^\top=\hat C_a$.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed EAKF update matrix $\hat A^{(3)}$ does not implement the moment-matching EAKF update it is presented as; nothing else in the paper uses this formula.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We can choose a norm with $\|A_s\|<1$  by Lemma \ref{lem:B_op_norm_bound}  since $\rho(A_s) < 1$.  Define $\mathcal T(\mu):=(A_s)_\#\mu * \text{Law}(U_s)$ on the metric space $(\mathcal P_2(V_s), W_2)$

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:B_op_norm_bound provides a weighted Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_P$, equivalent but not equal to the Euclidean norm, in which $\|A_s\|_P<1$. The pushforward $\mu\mapsto(A_s)_\#\mu$ is Lipschitz with constant $\|A_s\|_P$ only for the Wasserstein distance induced by $\|\cdot\|_P$; for the Euclidean $W_2$ on $(\mathcal P_2(V_s),W_2)$ (the metric named in the proof and defined in the notation section), the Lipschitz constant is the Euclidean operator norm, which can exceed 1 even when $\rho(A_s)<1$. Hence the claimed strict contraction of $\mathcal T$ on $(\mathcal P_2(V_s),W_2)$ is not established, and the uniqueness-in-law claim (a) of thm:main_result is unproven as written. The conclusion is correct and repairable by running Banach's theorem in the complete, Lipschitz-equivalent weighted Wasserstein metric (the fixed-point set is metric-independent).

failure_location.quote: Pushforward by $A_s$ is $W_2$-Lipschitz with constant $\|A_s\|<1$ and convolution is 1-Lipschitz, so $\mathcal T$ is a strict contraction; by Banach's fixed-point theorem, there is a unique fixed point $\mu_s$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $W_2$ by the Wasserstein distance $W_2^{(P)}$ induced by $\|\cdot\|_P$ (complete on $\Pp_2(V_s)$, same convergent sequences, same fixed points of $\mathcal T$), verify $\mathcal T$ is a $q$-contraction there with $q=\|A_s\|_P<1$, and conclude uniqueness of the fixed point, noting that the fixed-point set does not depend on which of the two equivalent metrics is used.
issues.overall_effect: Claim (a) of thm:main_result (unique solution in law of the stable block) lacks a valid proof as written; thm:enkf_update_unique part (2), thm:F_char, and cor:enkf_char invoke claim (a) to identify the stable-block solution with the fixed-point series and inherit the gap.
issues.title: Banach fixed-point argument in Theorem main_result conflates the equivalent norm with the Euclidean $W_2$ metric
issues.why_classification: A short, local repair of one metric in one proof step; the theorem's statement, the series representation, and all downstream conclusions survive unchanged.
